content.title: Masters 2013: A viewer's guide to coverage
content.text: April 4, 2013, 10:03 a.m. ETThis year's Masters will once again provide expansive viewing options to golf fans around the world.Live Masters coverage will be available on ESPN during the Par 3 Contest on Wednesday, April 10, from 3-5 p.m. Eastern. ESPN will also broadcast the tournament from 3-7:30 p.m. on Thursday, April 11, and Friday, April 12. CBS will again provide weekend coverage, including 30 additional minutes on Saturday, April 13, from 3-7 p.m. The fourth round is scheduled to air from 2-7 p.m. on Sunday, April 14.The Masters is expected to be broadcast live in more than 200 countries. Additionally, the Armed Forces Radio and Television Service will be broadcasting the event to U.S. military installations throughout the world.ESPN will also distribute 12 hours of live 3D programming during the Tournament on its ESPN 3D network.The CBS Sports Network will broadcast Masters On the Range, a live, two-hour show that features analysis and commentary April 8-14 from the Tournament Practice Area at Augusta National Golf Club.On the Internet, Masters.com is now active and will be regularly updated with stories, photos and on-demand video.During Masters week, the key features of the site will also include:• Seven live video channels, all available in HD-quality• Exclusive live scoring with integrated leader board highlights• Comprehensive news coverage, highlights, scores, statistics and player informationThe Masters has released free apps for iPhone, iPad, iPod touch and Android-based smartphones and tablets. All apps feature live scoring, several channels of live video content, pairings, news and video-on-demand highlights.For the complete schedule of live video on all platforms, please visit Masters.com.
